title: Kernel-intersection criterion for graph-admissible Lie algebras
statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional minimal-graph-admissible Lie algebra associated with a minimal graph $G(V,E)$, with $\dim(\mathfrak{g})\geq 2$, and let $\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{(\ell)}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ be the matrices and index set used in the source. **Kernel-intersection conjecture.** If

$$
\bigcap_{\ell\in\mathcal{N}}\operatorname{Ker}\{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{(\ell)}\}=\{0\},
$$

then no proper non-empty subset $W\subsetneq V$ satisfies the ideal graph property and spans a non-solvable ideal of $\mathfrak{g}$. The conjecture is presented as a refinement related to the preceding center and solvable-ideal conjecture; its general validity is unresolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16161

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “We now present a selection of open problems and conjectures that naturally arise from our findings.”
source_name: Tim Heib and David Edward Bruschi, “On the structural properties of Lie algebras via associated labeled directed graphs”, arXiv:2601.16161 (2026).
